findings.claim: Local governance is evaluated against the host safe display instead of the frozen validated tool arguments, which can bypass argument-sensitive deny/approval rules.
findings.evidence: The gate unwraps the prepared invocation, then replaces the previous tool arguments with `let arguments_json = action_display.to_string();` before the governance decision path; acceptance criterion 2.1 requires carrying frozen arguments through governance and 2.3 requires restrictive composition.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `serde_json::to_string(&invocation.validated_arguments)` for governance evaluation and keep `action_display` only for renderer/approval display.

findings.claim: Gate A1 is not a production-path integration boundary because it instantiates `UarHostToolAdmission` directly instead of exercising the Boss bridge plus UAR adapter path.
findings.evidence: The gate imports and constructs `new UarHostToolAdmission(...)` directly and posts to its handler; acceptance criterion 2.5 requires 'one production-path integration boundary' after the full slice is wired, and criterion 2.2 specifically requires the existing Boss bridge listener and UAR adapter contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the gate through `createUarHostMcpBridge` and the UAR HTTP admission adapter/managed MCP dispatch path so prepare, resolve, metadata injection, claim, and bridge authentication are exercised together.

findings.claim: New user-facing approval failure text is added without any locale updates, leaving the changed UI text untranslated.
findings.evidence: The diff adds the emitted error text `The tool approval no longer matches the prepared host admission`; acceptance criterion 2.4 requires 'translate all changed text across existing locales', but the diff contains no locale/resource updates.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the new approval/admission error strings into the existing localization resources and update all supported locales, or reuse an existing localized error key.
